newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-IMMEDIATE BAN TO FOLLOW POSITIVE DRUG TEST.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-IMMEDIATE BAN TO FOLLOW POSITIVE DRUG TEST.

text.p: Athletics chiefs closed a loophole in their fight against drug cheats on Saturday when they ruled that all competitors testing positive would be banned immediately.

International Amateur Athletic Federation (IAAF) president Primo Nebiolo said: "If a federation is reluctant to act immediately in accordance with IAAF rules, then the IAAF Council will from now on suspend the athlete until the national federation decides (a ban or not)."
The IAAF decision was prompted by what it considered to be the sluggish handling of the doping cases involving Americans Sandra Farmer-Patrick and Mary Slaney by the U.S. Track and Field Association.

IAAF general secretary Istvan Gyulai said in Monaco earlier this month that it was unacceptable that it had taken nearly a year for the U.S. national body to ban Farmer-Patrick for four years after she tested positive for the steroid testosterone.
Farmer-Patrick ran in the Atlanta Olympics last August despite the positive test because the case had not been concluded.
Slaney's case is not yet over. She was found to have high levels of testosterone in her body at the U.S. trials last June.

Under IAAF rules, athletes are banned immediately after the positive test pending an inquiry. But under U.S regulations an athlete is not suspended until the competitor has had time to have a hearing, if required.
